function: Excluded (above_phy), pp. 2, 8, 11: hierarchical RL learns UAV trajectory planning (UAV-to-cluster assignment) and UAV-SN association per TDMA step; no transmit power, bandwidth, or beam is learned.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Passes source_type, survey and no_learning (pointer-network and actor-critic agents trained by RL). Fails above_phy. p. 2: "perform resource allocation at a small timescale by controlling the association between UAVs and SNs". p. 8: Pointer-TP "outputs the index of the cluster assigned to each UAV per time slot k". p. 11: "The RA agent determines the association between the UAV and the SNs in the assigned cluster at each time step" (one-hot SN choice). These are UAV trajectory/placement and user association/scheduling. The paper calls the second decision resource allocation (time per SN is the sum of association indicators, eq. (10), p. 5), but no physical-layer quantity is learned: SN power P_m is a given parameter (p. 4), p. 5: "the transmission power is a constant denoted as Pc", and the bandwidth is fixed at 1 MHz (Table I, p. 12). So the aerial-link exception for learned power, resource allocation, or beams does not apply. This is borderline: if the reviewer reads the TDMA association as aerial-link resource allocation, the work would fall in area 6 (NTN admits single-antenna links).
